components.note: 刀 (knife) — cutting, as in 切, 刻, 到: a blade splits.
八 (eight) — originally two lines pulling apart: divide. 分 also gives 份 fèn, 粉 fěn and 纷 fēn.
酉 (wine jar) — marks wine and brewing, as in 酒, 醉 drunk, 醒; 配 first meant mixing wine, then matching.
己 (jǐ) is only a loose sound hint for pèi.

example.hanzi: 老师把任务分配给了每个小组。
example.pinyin: Lǎoshī bǎ rènwù fēnpèi gěile měi gè xiǎozǔ.
example.english: The teacher distributed the tasks to each group.
example.fact: Computer operating systems constantly perform their own version of resource distribution, called scheduling, deciding in fractions of a millisecond which of dozens of running programs gets the processor's attention next, using algorithms with names like 'round robin' and 'shortest job first.' Vilfredo Pareto's 1896 observation that roughly 80% of Italy's land was owned by 20% of the population led to the now-famous 80/20 rule, a pattern of uneven distribution that shows up again and again in wealth, web traffic, and even earthquake sizes. Ration books, a wartime tool for distributing scarce food and goods fairly, were used by Britain from 1940 all the way until 1954, nine years after World War II actually ended.

examples.hanzi: 公司按照工作量分配奖金。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī ànzhào gōngzuòliàng fēnpèi jiǎngjīn.
examples.english: The company allocates bonuses according to workload.

examples.hanzi: 毕业后，他被分配到上海工作。
examples.pinyin: Bìyè hòu, tā bèi fēnpèi dào Shànghǎi gōngzuò.
examples.english: After graduation, he was assigned to work in Shanghai.

components.note: 壴 (drum) — a festive drum, hence joyful and excellent; the top of 鼓 gǔ drum.
加 (jiā) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 架 jià, 驾 jià and 贺 hè.
宀 (roof) — a guest under your roof; also in 家 home, 客 guest.
兵 (bīng) gives a close sound; 滨 bīn and 摈 bìn share the part.

example.hanzi: 今晚的婚礼邀请了很多嘉宾。
example.pinyin: Jīnwǎn de hūnlǐ yāoqǐngle hěnduō jiābīn.
example.english: Tonight's wedding invited many honored guests.
example.fact: The tradition of a guest of honor sitting at the head of a banquet table traces back to medieval European feasts, where seating position at the 'high table' directly signaled social rank, with the most honored guests placed nearest the host and the salt cellar, the origin of the phrase 'below the salt' for lower-status guests. Japanese tea ceremony etiquette assigns the guest of honor a specific role called 'shokyaku,' who sits closest to the host and is expected to ask particular ceremonial questions on behalf of the group. Television award shows and talk shows formalized a modern version of the honored guest, with green rooms and pre-show briefings designed specifically to make a featured guest comfortable before facing an audience.

examples.hanzi: 今天的嘉宾是一位著名的作家。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān de jiābīn shì yī wèi zhùmíng de zuòjiā.
examples.english: Today's guest is a famous writer.

examples.hanzi: 请各位嘉宾入座，宴会马上开始。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng gèwèi jiābīn rùzuò, yànhuì mǎshàng kāishǐ.
examples.english: Honored guests, please take your seats, the banquet is about to begin.

components.note: 亻 (person) — a person bowing low; also in 他 he, 们 plural.
氐 (dī) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 底 dǐ and 抵 dǐ.
亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 位; 估 is a trader's guess at value.
古 (gǔ) is a close sound clue; same part in 姑 gū, 枯 kū, 苦 kǔ.

example.hanzi: 千万不要低估这个对手的实力。
example.pinyin: Qiānwàn bùyào dīgū zhège duìshǒu de shílì.
example.english: Whatever you do, don't underestimate this opponent's strength.
example.fact: Early 20th-century engineers underestimated the risk of resonance in bridge design, a miscalculation dramatically exposed when the Tacoma Narrows Bridge in Washington State twisted itself apart in 40 mph winds in 1940, a collapse caught on film and still studied in engineering classrooms today. Meteorologists in 1900 severely underestimated an approaching hurricane's strength, contributing to the Galveston, Texas disaster that killed an estimated 6,000 to 12,000 people, still the deadliest natural disaster in US history. Cognitive psychologists have documented a specific bias called the 'planning fallacy,' where people reliably underestimate how long tasks will take even when they have accurate data from past similar projects.

examples.hanzi: 不要低估孩子学习的能力。
examples.pinyin: Bù yào dīgū háizi xuéxí de nénglì.
examples.english: Don't underestimate children's ability to learn.

examples.hanzi: 我低估了路上堵车的时间，结果迟到了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ dīgū le lùshang dǔchē de shíjiān, jiéguǒ chídào le.
examples.english: I underestimated the traffic time and ended up late.

components.note: 艹 (plants) — marks grasses and flowers, as in 草, 茶, 菜; 花 is a flower.
化 (huà) hints at the sound: 花 huā is close, and 化 also gives 华 huá and 货 huò.
土 (earth) — a green shoot pushing up from the ground: growth, birth, life. 生 also sounds out 性 xìng, 姓 xìng and 星 xīng.

example.hanzi: 这道菜里加了很多花生碎。
example.pinyin: Zhè dào cài lǐ jiāle hěnduō huāshēngsuì.
example.english: This dish has a lot of crushed peanuts added to it.
example.fact: Peanuts are not true nuts but legumes, growing underground after their flowers bend down and bury themselves in soil to develop, a process called geocarpy that is rare among cultivated crops. George Washington Carver, working at Tuskegee Institute in the early 20th century, developed over 300 documented uses for the peanut, from cooking oil to dyes, as part of an effort to help Southern farmers diversify away from soil-depleting cotton monoculture. Peanut allergies, among the most common and potentially severe food allergies, affect roughly 2% of children in the United States, and researchers have found that early, controlled introduction of peanuts in infancy can significantly reduce the risk of developing the allergy.

examples.hanzi: 我对花生过敏，不能吃这道菜。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ duì huāshēng guòmǐn, bù néng chī zhè dào cài.
examples.english: I'm allergic to peanuts and can't eat this dish.

examples.hanzi: 奶奶用花生榨出了香喷喷的油。
examples.pinyin: Nǎinai yòng huāshēng zhà chū le xiāngpēnpēn de yóu.
examples.english: Grandma pressed fragrant oil from peanuts.

components.note: 糸 (silk, simplified 纟) — dyed cloth, hence colours; also in 红 red, 绿 green.
此 (cǐ) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 柴 chái and 雌 cí.
⺈ (bent person) — a person's figure, the top part of 色. Old story: a person (⺈) sitting on 巴 shows how feelings colour the face, hence 'colour, look'; treat as a memory aid.
巴 (bā) — the lower part; dictionary reads the pair as 'what a person desires'. Memory aid: a face reddening with feeling is a 'colour'.

example.hanzi: 她穿了一条紫色的裙子。
example.pinyin: Tā chuānle yì tiáo zǐsè de qúnzi.
example.english: She wore a purple skirt.
example.fact: For most of history, purple dye was extraordinarily expensive because Tyrian purple, the ancient Mediterranean standard, required crushing thousands of small sea snails to produce even a single gram, making the color a status symbol reserved for royalty in Rome and Byzantium. The modern synthetic dye industry began accidentally in 1856, when 18-year-old chemist William Perkin, trying to synthesize the malaria drug quinine, instead produced a vivid purple compound he called mauveine. In visible light, purple sits at the boundary of what human eyes can perceive, and true violet light of a single wavelength looks noticeably different from the reddish-blue 'purple' our brains construct by mixing red and blue signals.

examples.hanzi: 紫色是我最喜欢的颜色。
examples.pinyin: Zǐsè shì wǒ zuì xǐhuan de yánsè.
examples.english: Purple is my favorite color.

examples.hanzi: 天空在日落时变成了紫色。
examples.pinyin: Tiānkōng zài rìluò shí biànchéng le zǐsè.
examples.english: The sky turned purple at sunset.

components.note: 凵 (open pit) — oldest form shows a foot stepping out of a pit or cave: to go out, come out.
⻊ (foot, form of 足) — feet and travel: 跑, 跳, 跟; 路 is a road.
各 (gè) is a loose sound clue; same part in 洛 luò, 落 luò, 客 kè.

example.hanzi: 面对经济危机，政府急需找到一条出路。
example.pinyin: Miànduì jīngjì wēijī, zhèngfǔ jíxū zhǎodào yì tiáo chūlù.
example.english: Facing the economic crisis, the government urgently needs to find a way out.
example.fact: The Apollo 13 mission in 1970 became a defining case study of finding a way out of a seemingly hopeless situation, after an oxygen tank explosion crippled the spacecraft and ground engineers had to improvise a carbon dioxide scrubber from spare parts, duct tape, and a plastic bag to keep the crew alive during their return to Earth. Maze-solving algorithms like the 'right-hand rule,' where a solver simply keeps one hand on the wall at all times, are mathematically guaranteed to find an exit from any simply connected maze, though they can fail in mazes with disconnected loops. Urban planners studying building fires have found that clearly marked, well-lit exit routes reduce evacuation time far more than adding extra exits, since panicked crowds tend to follow visible cues rather than search independently.

examples.hanzi: 大学毕业生的出路越来越多样了。
examples.pinyin: Dàxué bìyèshēng de chūlù yuèláiyuè duōyàng le.
examples.english: The career paths for university graduates are becoming more varied.

examples.hanzi: 山里的路被堵死了，我们找不到出路。
examples.pinyin: Shān lǐ de lù bèi dǔ sǐ le, wǒmen zhǎo bù dào chūlù.
examples.english: The mountain path was blocked and we couldn't find a way out.

components.note: 纟 (silk, thread) — 纟 is the simplified 糸 (thread), as in 红, 给; 纪 first meant the thread end, then keeping record, as in 世纪.
己 (jǐ) — same sound, different tone — 纪 is jì; 己 also sounds out 记 jì.
心 (heart) — 心 marks thoughts and feelings, as in 想, 思, 感; 念 is to think of someone.
今 (jīn) — loose hint — 念 is niàn; 今 also sounds out 琴 qín and 含 hán, and means "now".
日 (sun, day) — a picture of the sun, once round with a dot, now squared off. As a radical it marks light and time: 明, 晴, 时.

example.hanzi: 今天是他们结婚十周年的纪念日。
example.pinyin: Jīntiān shì tāmen jiéhūn shí zhōunián de jìniànrì.
example.english: Today is their tenth wedding anniversary.
example.fact: The United States' Memorial Day traces back to 'Decoration Day,' first widely observed in 1868 to honor Civil War dead by decorating their graves with flowers, and it wasn't fixed as a federal holiday on the last Monday of May until 1971. Japan's Hiroshima Peace Memorial Ceremony is held every August 6th at 8:15 a.m., the exact minute the atomic bomb detonated in 1945, with a moment of silence observed at that precise time each year. Some memorial observances are tied to the original event's timing rather than a fixed calendar date; Anzac Day in Australia and New Zealand includes pre-dawn services timed to echo the original 1915 Gallipoli landing, which began before sunrise.

examples.hanzi: 今天是我们的结婚纪念日，我订了餐厅。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān shì wǒmen de jiéhūn jìniànrì, wǒ dìng le cāntīng.
examples.english: Today is our wedding anniversary, so I booked a restaurant.

examples.hanzi: 这个纪念日对我来说意义重大。
examples.pinyin: Zhège jìniànrì duì wǒ lái shuō yìyì zhòngdà.
examples.english: This anniversary means a lot to me.

components.note: 力 (strength) — effort and motion, as in 办, 助, 努. The part 云 stands in for 重 in the traditional 動, which was the sound clue.
⺼ (flesh, 肉月旁) — body parts, as in 脸 face, 肝 liver; 脉 is the network of vessels branching through the body.

example.hanzi: 医生说他的动脉出现了轻微堵塞。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng shuō tā de dòngmài chūxiànle qīngwēi dǔsè.
example.english: The doctor said his artery showed slight blockage.
example.fact: Arteries carry blood away from the heart under high pressure, which is why their walls are thick and muscular compared to the thinner, floppier walls of veins that return blood at low pressure. The aorta, the body's largest artery, has a diameter roughly the size of a garden hose in adults and must flex with every heartbeat for an entire lifetime, over 2.5 billion times on average, without failing. Atherosclerosis, the buildup of fatty plaque inside artery walls, was long assumed to be purely a modern lifestyle disease, but CT scans of Egyptian, Peruvian, and other ancient mummies in a 2013 study found hardened arteries in roughly a third of specimens across very different diets and eras.

examples.hanzi: 心脏通过动脉把血液送到全身。
examples.pinyin: Xīnzàng tōngguò dòngmài bǎ xuèyè sòng dào quánshēn.
examples.english: The heart sends blood to the whole body through the arteries.

examples.hanzi: 高速公路是这个国家交通的大动脉。
examples.pinyin: Gāosù gōnglù shì zhège guójiā jiāotōng de dà dòngmài.
examples.english: The highway is the main artery of this country's transport.

components.note: 页 (head, page) — in traditional 頭 (豆 + 页): 页 is an old picture of a head, as in 顶, 领, 额. 头 dropped both parts.
大 (big) — the bottom. Memory aid: a big 大 body with two dots ⺀ like eyes above — the head, as in 头发. The dictionary's reading is loose.
骨 (bone) — 骨 is the bone radical, as in 骼, 髓, 体; 骨 is bones, with ⺼ (flesh) beneath.

example.hanzi: 考古学家在遗址中发现了一个古人的头骨。
example.pinyin: Kǎogǔ xuéjiā zài yízhǐ zhōng fāxiànle yí gè gǔrén de tóugǔ.
example.english: Archaeologists discovered an ancient person's skull at the site.
example.fact: The adult human skull is made of 22 separate bones fused together along jagged seams called sutures, but a newborn's skull bones remain unfused and slightly overlapping, letting the head compress and pass through the birth canal before fusing fully over the following months and years. The Homo naledi remains discovered in South Africa's Rising Star cave system in 2013 belonged to a small-brained hominin species that nonetheless appears to have deliberately placed its dead deep in a nearly inaccessible chamber, challenging assumptions about which human relatives were capable of ritual behavior. Forensic anthropologists can estimate a skull's age, sex, and ancestry from measurements alone, a technique that has helped identify remains in mass disasters and historical burial sites worldwide.

examples.hanzi: 博物馆里展出了一个恐龙的头骨。
examples.pinyin: Bówùguǎn lǐ zhǎnchū le yī gè kǒnglóng de tóugǔ.
examples.english: The museum displays a dinosaur skull.

examples.hanzi: 他摔倒时撞到了头，医生担心头骨骨折。
examples.pinyin: Tā shuāidǎo shí zhuàng dào le tóu, yīshēng dānxīn tóugǔ gǔzhé.
examples.english: He hit his head in the fall, and the doctor worried about a skull fracture.

components.note: 廾 (two hands) — in 開 two hands lift the bar of a gate; 开 is the simplified shape. Compare 关 (close).
广 (shelter) — buildings, as in 店, 床, 度: a hall or courtyard.
廷 (tíng) gives the exact sound; also in 挺 tǐng and 艇 tǐng.

example.hanzi: 这起案件将于下周一开庭审理。
example.pinyin: Zhè qǐ ànjiàn jiāng yú xià zhōuyī kāitíng shěnlǐ.
example.english: This case will go to trial next Monday.
example.fact: The Nuremberg trials, which opened court proceedings on November 20, 1945, were the first international tribunal to prosecute state leaders for war crimes and crimes against humanity, establishing legal precedents still cited in international courts today. The longest criminal trial in US history, the McMartin preschool abuse case, remained in court proceedings from 1987 to 1990 without a single conviction, at a cost exceeding 15 million dollars. Some countries, including the United Kingdom, still open certain court sessions with elaborate ceremonial traditions, such as judges wearing wigs dating back to 17th-century fashion trends that simply never fell out of use in the legal profession.

examples.hanzi: 法院明天上午九点开庭。
examples.pinyin: Fǎyuàn míngtiān shàngwǔ jiǔ diǎn kāitíng.
examples.english: The court will begin its session at nine tomorrow morning.

examples.hanzi: 开庭前，律师仔细检查了所有的材料。
examples.pinyin: Kāitíng qián, lǜshī zǐxì jiǎnchá le suǒyǒu de cáiliào.
examples.english: Before the hearing, the lawyer carefully checked all the documents.

meanings: to have as a feature or characteristic

components.note: 巾 (cloth) — cloth, as in 布, 帽, 帮: a belt of cloth with pieces hanging from it.
月 (flesh/meat, not moon here) — oldest form is a hand holding a piece of meat, "to possess"; 月 as meat also appears in 肉 words like 肚 belly and 脑 brain.

example.hanzi: 这份报告带有明显的偏见。
example.pinyin: Zhè fèn bàogào dàiyǒu míngxiǎn de piānjiàn.
example.english: This report carries an obvious bias.
example.fact: Cognitive bias research identifies dozens of systematic patterns that reports, decisions, and even scientific studies can carry without their authors realizing it; confirmation bias alone, the tendency to favor information that supports an existing belief, has been documented in controlled experiments since the 1960s. Peer review in scientific publishing was formalized specifically to catch bias and error before a paper carries the weight of publication, though studies of the process itself have found it still lets some biased or flawed papers through. Some diseases are literally carried without symptoms; 'Typhoid Mary' Mallon, an asymptomatic carrier of typhoid fever in early 20th-century New York, unknowingly infected dozens of people while working as a cook, before public health officials understood a person could carry a disease without ever appearing sick.

examples.hanzi: 这道菜带有淡淡的柠檬香味。
examples.pinyin: Zhè dào cài dàiyǒu dàndàn de níngméng xiāngwèi.
examples.english: This dish carries a light lemon fragrance.

examples.hanzi: 这个包装盒上带有一个红色的标志。
examples.pinyin: Zhège bāozhuānghé shàng dàiyǒu yī gè hóngsè de biāozhì.
examples.english: This packaging box has a red logo on it.

components.note: 瓜 (melon) — a melon hanging from a vine. It lends its sound to 孤 gū and 狐 hú, besides 傻瓜 and 南瓜.

example.hanzi: 夏天我喜欢吃西瓜。
example.pinyin: Xiàtiān wǒ xǐhuan chī xīguā.
example.english: In summer I like to eat watermelon.
example.fact: 瓜 covers the melon and gourd family: 西瓜 (watermelon), 黄瓜 (cucumber), 南瓜 (pumpkin). 吃瓜群众 ('melon-eating crowd') is slang for bystanders watching gossip.

examples.hanzi: 这个西瓜又大又甜。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xīguā yòu dà yòu tián.
examples.english: This watermelon is big and sweet.

examples.hanzi: 我晚饭做了一盘黄瓜。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ wǎnfàn zuò le yì pán huángguā.
examples.english: I made a plate of cucumber for dinner.

components.note: 扌 (hand, 提手旁) — marks hand actions, as in 打 hit, 推 push, 拉 pull; 掏 is reaching in and taking out.
匋 (táo) — close sound: 掏 tāo. 匋 also sounds out 陶 táo and 淘 táo.

example.hanzi: 他从口袋里掏出手机。
example.pinyin: Tā cóng kǒudài lǐ tāochū shǒujī.
example.english: He pulled his phone out of his pocket.
example.fact: 掏 is colloquial. 掏钱 means 'to pay up', also 掏腰包; 掏耳朵 is to clean your ears; 掏心窝 means to speak from the heart.

examples.hanzi: 他伸手掏口袋，找钥匙。
examples.pinyin: Tā shēnshǒu tāo kǒudài, zhǎo yàoshi.
examples.english: He reached into his pocket to look for the keys.

examples.hanzi: 我今天掏了不少钱买礼物。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jīntiān tāo le bù shǎo qián mǎi lǐwù.
examples.english: I paid quite a lot of money for gifts today.

components.note: 人 (person) — the top. Common reading: a person standing between two sides, a go-between, as in 介绍 to introduce. Early forms may be armour.
八 (eight, divide) — Dictionary: a border dividing people. Memory aid: a person in the middle of two divided parts — in between.

example.hanzi: 请允许我介绍一下自己。
example.pinyin: Qǐng yǔnxǔ wǒ jièshào yíxià zìjǐ.
example.english: Please allow me to introduce myself.
example.fact: 介 appears in 介绍 (introduce), 介意 (to mind, as in 别介意), 中介 (agent) and 媒介 (medium). It is also a measure word in the literary 一介书生 ('a mere scholar').

examples.hanzi: 我来给你介绍一下我的朋友。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ lái gěi nǐ jièshào yíxià wǒ de péngyou.
examples.english: Let me introduce my friend to you.

examples.hanzi: 这本书的内容简介很吸引人。
examples.pinyin: Zhè běn shū de nèiróng jiǎnjiè hěn xīyǐn rén.
examples.english: The brief summary of this book is very appealing.

components.note: 鬼 (ghost) — spirits and the unseen: 魔 demon, 魅 charm, 魄 spirit; 魂 is the soul.
云 (yún) is a near sound match for hún.

example.hanzi: 他吓得魂都飞了。
example.pinyin: Tā xià de hún dōu fēi le.
example.english: He was so scared his soul flew out of him.
example.fact: 魂 is the ethereal soul. Traditional thought pairs it with 魄 (the bodily soul). 灵魂 is 'soul', 丢魂 'lose one's wits', and 魂 also appears in 民族魂 ('soul of a nation').

examples.hanzi: 他看起来像丢了魂一样。
examples.pinyin: Tā kàn qǐlái xiàng diū le hún yíyàng.
examples.english: He looks as if he has lost his soul.

examples.hanzi: 这个故事讲的是一个灵魂的旅行。
examples.pinyin: Zhège gùshi jiǎng de shì yí ge línghún de lǚxíng.
examples.english: This story is about a soul's journey.

components.note: 走 (walk, run) — marks movement on foot, as in 起 rise, 越 cross, 超 surpass; 赶 is chasing or hurrying to catch up.
干 (gān) — gives the sound — 赶 is gǎn, same syllable with a different tone; 秆 gǎn and 肝 gān share it.
回 (return) — a swirl or whirlpool drawn as nested squares: it turns around and comes back.

example.hanzi: 听到消息后，他立刻赶回家。
example.pinyin: Tīngdào xiāoxi hòu, tā lìkè gǎnhuí jiā.
example.english: After hearing the news, he rushed straight back home.
example.fact: In 1966, Formula One driver Jack Brabham had to rush back to a workshop mid-race weekend after a mechanical failure, and racing pit crews since then have trained specifically to minimize the seconds lost every time a driver must return unexpectedly. Migratory Arctic terns rush back to the same nesting grounds each year after completing the longest known migration of any animal, a round trip that can exceed 90,000 kilometers between the Arctic and Antarctic. Salmon undergo one of nature's most dramatic 'rushing back' journeys, swimming upstream against powerful currents to return to the exact river where they hatched years earlier, guided partly by a memorized magnetic and chemical signature of their home waters.

examples.hanzi: 会议一结束，我就赶回了公司。
examples.pinyin: Huìyì yī jiéshù, wǒ jiù gǎnhuí le gōngsī.
examples.english: As soon as the meeting ended, I rushed back to the company.

examples.hanzi: 我们必须在天黑前赶回村子。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen bìxū zài tiān hēi qián gǎnhuí cūnzi.
examples.english: We must hurry back to the village before dark.

components.note: ⻊ (foot, form of 足) — feet and travel: 跑, 跳, 跟; 路 is a road.
各 (gè) is a loose sound clue; same part in 洛 luò, 落 luò, 客 kè.
易 (yì) is a loose sound clue for 踢 tī, 赐 cì and 惕 tì; the meaning "easy" comes from "change" and its early lizard picture is unproven.
斤 (axe) — the original idea was chopping with an axe, as in 新, 斩 chop, 断 break; today 斯 is mostly a sound-borrowing syllable sī in foreign names like 俄罗斯.

example.hanzi: 路易斯是我们班上最会画画的学生。
example.pinyin: Lùyìsī shì wǒmen bān shàng zuì huì huàhuà de xuéshēng.
example.english: Louis is the best drawer in our class.
example.fact: The name Louis descends from the Old Frankish 'Hlodowig,' meaning 'famous warrior,' and was carried by eighteen kings of France, giving rise to the naming convention of 'Louis XIV' and similar regnal numbering used across European monarchies. Louis Pasteur developed pasteurization and the first vaccines for rabies and anthrax in the 19th century, work that helped found modern microbiology. Lewis and Clark, the American explorers who charted a route to the Pacific between 1804 and 1806, gave their combined names to a famous westward expedition, though the 'Lewis' in that pairing is the same name as 'Louis' in its English form.

examples.hanzi: 路易斯每天骑自行车上班。
examples.pinyin: Lùyìsī měitiān qí zìxíngchē shàngbān.
examples.english: Louis rides a bike to work every day.

examples.hanzi: 我很喜欢路易斯做的意大利面。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ hěn xǐhuan Lùyìsī zuò de Yìdàlì miàn.
examples.english: I really like the pasta that Louis makes.

components.note: 艹 (grass, plants) — 艹 marks plants — 艺 originally meant planting and cultivating, later skill and art.
乙 (yǐ) — near sound — 艺 is yì, same syllable with another tone.
術 (traditional) — 行 (road) plus 朮 (zhú) as sound: art, method. 术 is the sound part alone; same sound in 述 shù, as in 手术, 技术, 艺术.
口 (mouth) — three mouths: many goods and people speaking; hence products, quality, and to taste. Also in 品尝 and 作品.

example.hanzi: 这件艺术品在拍卖会上卖出了天价。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiàn yìshùpǐn zài pāimàihuì shàng màichūle tiānjià.
example.english: This work of art sold for an astronomical price at the auction.
example.fact: Leonardo da Vinci's 'Salvator Mundi' sold at a 2017 Christie's auction for 450.3 million dollars, making it the most expensive work of art ever sold at auction, though scholars still dispute how much of the painting was actually done by Leonardo's own hand versus his workshop. The Mona Lisa, arguably the most famous work of art in the world, has never been formally appraised or insured for a specific dollar value, since the Louvre considers it priceless and effectively unsellable. Art forensics labs now use techniques borrowed from particle physics, including X-ray fluorescence and infrared reflectography, to peer beneath a painting's visible surface and detect forgeries or earlier hidden compositions.

examples.hanzi: 这间屋子里摆满了各种艺术品。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiān wūzi lǐ bǎi mǎn le gèzhǒng yìshùpǐn.
examples.english: This room is filled with various works of art.

examples.hanzi: 他收藏艺术品已经三十年了。
examples.pinyin: Tā shōucáng yìshùpǐn yǐjīng sānshí nián le.
examples.english: He has been collecting art for thirty years.

components.note: 风 (fēng, wind) — in the oldest writing the phoenix and the wind shared one character, hence the similar look and sound (fèng / fēng).
皇 (huáng) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 煌 huáng, 惶 huáng and 蝗 huáng.

example.hanzi: 传说中，凤凰浴火之后能够重生。
example.pinyin: Chuánshuō zhōng, fènghuáng yùhuǒ zhīhòu nénggòu chóngshēng.
example.english: According to legend, the phoenix can be reborn after bathing in fire.
example.fact: The phoenix myth appears independently across multiple ancient cultures, from the Greek 'phoinix' described by Herodotus around 440 BC to the Chinese fenghuang and the Egyptian bennu bird associated with the sun god Ra, each imagining a bird tied to cyclical death and rebirth. Unlike the Western phoenix, the Chinese fenghuang was traditionally seen as a composite of multiple animals, and paired with the dragon it symbolized the empress the way the dragon symbolized the emperor, rather than being a single fire-bird archetype. The bird species most often cited as a phoenix inspiration is the flamingo, whose reddish-orange color, coastal habitat near the Mediterranean, and dramatic wingspan may have shaped ancient descriptions of a fiery, mythical bird.

examples.hanzi: 中国神话里，凤凰是吉祥的象征。
examples.pinyin: Zhōngguó shénhuà lǐ, fènghuáng shì jíxiáng de xiàngzhēng.
examples.english: In Chinese myth, the phoenix is a symbol of good luck.

examples.hanzi: 我们去了湖南的凤凰古城旅游。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen qù le Húnán de Fènghuáng gǔchéng lǚyóu.
examples.english: We traveled to Fenghuang Ancient Town in Hunan.

components.note: 彡 (patterns, hairlines) — marks shape, shadow and decoration, as in 影 shadow, 彩 colour; 形 is a shape.
开 (a worn-down 幵) hints at the sound: 形 xíng sounds like 刑 and 型.
力 (strength) — 力 is strength, as in 办, 动, 努; 势 is force or momentum.

example.hanzi: 目前的国际形势非常复杂。
example.pinyin: Mùqián de guójì xíngshì fēicháng fùzá.
example.english: The current international situation is extremely complex.
example.fact: Game theorists studying complex strategic situations often model them using 'the fog of war,' a term coined by Prussian military theorist Carl von Clausewitz in the 19th century to describe how uncertainty about an unfolding situation degrades even the best-laid plans. The Cuban Missile Crisis of 1962 is frequently studied as a textbook case of a rapidly shifting situation, where President Kennedy's advisors reportedly gave differing probability estimates, ranging from one-in-three to near-certain, for whether the standoff would escalate into nuclear war. Modern intelligence agencies use a formal system called 'situational awareness,' originally developed for fighter pilots needing to process fast-changing battlefield conditions, now applied broadly to everything from cybersecurity operations centers to emergency room triage.

examples.hanzi: 目前的经济形势对年轻人不太乐观。
examples.pinyin: Mùqián de jīngjì xíngshì duì niánqīngrén bù tài lèguān.
examples.english: The current economic situation is not very optimistic for young people.

examples.hanzi: 比赛进入了最后阶段，形势对我们很有利。
examples.pinyin: Bǐsài jìnrù le zuìhòu jiēduàn, xíngshì duì wǒmen hěn yǒulì.
examples.english: The game entered its final stage and the situation is very favorable to us.

meanings: to coerce (sb into doing sth bad)

components.note: 弓 (bow) — the vertical stroke 丨 is the string being drawn back on a bow — 引 is to pull, then to attract and to cite.
讠 (speech, from 言) — marks talk, as in 说, 话, 请; 诱 is to coax with words.
秀 (xiù) hints at the sound: 诱 yòu is close to 透 tòu and 锈 xiù.

example.hanzi: 毒品贩子想引诱那个孩子上钩。
example.pinyin: Dúpǐn fànzi xiǎng yǐnyòu nàge háizi shàng gōu.
example.english: The drug dealer wanted to lure that child into a trap.
example.fact: The Venus flytrap lures insects with a sweet-smelling nectar secreted along the rim of its hinged leaves; once an insect brushes two trigger hairs within about 20 seconds of each other, the trap snaps shut in under a tenth of a second — one of the fastest movements in the plant kingdom.

examples.hanzi: 小心陌生人用糖果引诱孩子。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎoxīn mòshēngrén yòng tángguǒ yǐnyòu háizi.
examples.english: Beware of strangers luring children with candy.

examples.hanzi: 香味引诱着路过的行人走进面包店。
examples.pinyin: Xiāngwèi yǐnyòu zhe lùguò de xíngrén zǒu jìn miànbāodiàn.
examples.english: The aroma tempted passersby into the bakery.

components.note: 山 (mountain) — a picture of three peaks; as a radical it marks hills, as in 岛, 峰, 岸.
羊 — a sheep's head with curved horns; the sheep radical, as in 美 beautiful, 群 flock. It also sounds out 样 yàng and 养 yǎng.

example.hanzi: 那只山羊爬到了陡峭的岩石上。
example.pinyin: Nà zhī shānyáng pá dào le dǒuqiào de yánshí shàng.
example.english: That goat climbed onto the steep rocks.
example.fact: Mountain goats have cloven hooves with an inner pad that acts like a suction cup, letting them grip near-vertical rock faces and cross cliffs over 1,000 feet tall. Wild goats were among the first animals domesticated by humans, around 10,000 years ago in the Zagros Mountains of present-day Iran.

examples.hanzi: 农场里养着几只白色的山羊。
examples.pinyin: Nóngchǎng lǐ yǎng zhe jǐ zhī báisè de shānyáng.
examples.english: The farm raises several white goats.

examples.hanzi: 山羊的奶可以做成奶酪。
examples.pinyin: Shānyáng de nǎi kěyǐ zuò chéng nǎilào.
examples.english: Goat's milk can be made into cheese.

meanings: to see with one's own eyes

components.note: 目 (eye) — an eye turned on its side. As a radical it marks sight: 看 look, 眼 eye, 睡 sleep, 盯 stare.
目 (eye) — looking at something; also in 看 look, 眼 eye.
者 (zhě) is a loose clue; 赌 dǔ and 堵 dǔ share it and sound exactly like 睹.

example.hanzi: 许多市民目睹了那场车祸的发生。
example.pinyin: Xǔduō shìmín mùdǔ le nà chǎng chēhuò de fāshēng.
example.english: Many residents witnessed that car accident happen.
example.fact: Eyewitness memory is far less reliable than most people assume — the Innocence Project has found that mistaken eyewitness identification played a role in more than 60% of the wrongful convictions later overturned by DNA evidence in the United States.

examples.hanzi: 我亲眼目睹了他们吵架的全过程。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ qīnyǎn mùdǔ le tāmen chǎojià de quán guòchéng.
examples.english: I saw the whole argument with my own eyes.

examples.hanzi: 没有人愿意目睹这样的悲剧再次发生。
examples.pinyin: Méiyǒu rén yuànyì mùdǔ zhèyàng de bēijù zàicì fāshēng.
examples.english: No one wants to witness such a tragedy happen again.

components.note: 氵 (water) — marks water, as in 河, 海, 游; 潜 is to dive under the water, hence hidden, as in 潜水.
土 (earth) — ground and place, as in 地 earth, 坐 sit; 在 is "to be at a place".
才 (cái) is a close sound clue for zài; 才 also appears in 材 cái.

example.hanzi: 科学家正在研究这种药物的潜在副作用。
example.pinyin: Kēxuéjiā zhèngzài yánjiū zhè zhǒng yàowù de qiánzài fùzuòyòng.
example.english: Scientists are researching the potential side effects of this drug.
example.fact: Penicillin was discovered in 1928 when Alexander Fleming noticed that mold accidentally contaminating a petri dish was killing the bacteria around it. He almost threw the dish away, not immediately recognizing its potential — it would go on to save an estimated 200 million lives.

examples.hanzi: 这家公司有很大的潜在客户群。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī yǒu hěn dà de qiánzài kèhù qún.
examples.english: This company has a large base of potential customers.

examples.hanzi: 我们必须找出系统中的潜在问题。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen bìxū zhǎochū xìtǒng zhōng de qiánzài wèntí.
examples.english: We must find the potential problems in the system.

components.note: 心 (heart) — feelings: 想, 思, 感, 怕; 恶 is a bad heart, evil.
亚 (yà) is only a loose sound hint for è.
化 (change) — one person 亻 beside an upside-down person 匕 — a change of state; 化 is to change, as in 文化 and 变化.

example.hanzi: 病人的病情在夜里突然恶化了。
example.pinyin: Bìngrén de bìngqíng zài yèlǐ tūrán èhuà le.
example.english: The patient's condition suddenly worsened during the night.
example.fact: The Aral Sea, once the world's fourth-largest lake, has shrunk to about 10% of its original volume since the 1960s after Soviet irrigation projects diverted its feeder rivers, a decline environmental scientists often cite as one of the fastest man-made ecological disasters on record.

examples.hanzi: 天气恶化了，航班全部取消。
examples.pinyin: Tiānqì èhuà le, hángbān quánbù qǔxiāo.
examples.english: The weather worsened and all flights were canceled.

examples.hanzi: 两国的关系最近有所恶化。
examples.pinyin: Liǎng guó de guānxì zuìjìn yǒusuǒ èhuà.
examples.english: Relations between the two countries have recently deteriorated.

components.note: 纟 (thread, simplified 糸) — silk and cord words: 红 red, 给 give, 线 line; a thread has an end, which fits 终 end.
冬 (dōng) rhymes with 终 zhōng, and 冬 originally meant the end (of the year) too — so it helps sound and sense.
木 (tree) — wood, as in 树, 林, 桌: 极 first meant a roof beam, the very top.
及 (jí) gives the exact sound; also in 级 jí and 吸 xī.

example.hanzi: 这场比赛被称为两位棋手的终极对决。
example.pinyin: Zhè chǎng bǐsài bèi chēng wéi liǎng wèi qíshǒu de zhōngjí duìjué.
example.english: This match was called the ultimate showdown between the two chess players.
example.fact: Physicists sometimes describe the search for a single theory unifying gravity with quantum mechanics as the field's 'ultimate' goal. Albert Einstein spent the last three decades of his life chasing such a unified field theory and never succeeded — the problem remains unsolved today.

examples.hanzi: 这是一道终极难题，没人能解开。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yī dào zhōngjí nántí, méi rén néng jiě kāi.
examples.english: This is an ultimate puzzle that no one can solve.

examples.hanzi: 他的终极目标是成为一名医生。
examples.pinyin: Tā de zhōngjí mùbiāo shì chéngwéi yī míng yīshēng.
examples.english: His ultimate goal is to become a doctor.

components.note: 刂 (knife) — cutting, as in 到, 分, 刻; to cut apart means separate.
另 (lìng, other) — separating things into "other" parts: 别 is another, different, or "don't".
夂 (foot) — stopping or going: 处 first meant to stay or settle, then a place or to deal with.

example.hanzi: 这里没有空房间了,你得去别处看看。
example.pinyin: Zhèlǐ méiyǒu kōng fángjiān le, nǐ děi qù biéchù kànkan.
example.english: There are no empty rooms here, you'll have to look elsewhere.
example.fact: Monarch butterflies that hatch in the United States and Canada each fall migrate up to 3,000 miles to a few specific fir-forested mountains in central Mexico, a journey no single butterfly completes twice — the return trip north is finished by their offspring instead.

examples.hanzi: 这家店没有货，我们去别处看看吧。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn méiyǒu huò, wǒmen qù biéchù kànkan ba.
examples.english: This shop is out of stock, so let's look elsewhere.

examples.hanzi: 他的心思好像在别处，没有听我说话。
examples.pinyin: Tā de xīnsi hǎoxiàng zài biéchù, méiyǒu tīng wǒ shuōhuà.
examples.english: His mind seems to be elsewhere, and he isn't listening to me.

components.note: 未 (not yet) — a tree 木 with a new short branch on top, still growing. Compare 末 mò (end/tip), where the top stroke is longer.
口 (mouth) — knowing is something you can say aloud; 口 sits in many speech words (问 ask, 告 tell).
矢 (shǐ, arrow) is only a loose sound clue today; the same 知 sound is in 智 zhì (wisdom).

example.hanzi: 地图上标出了一片未知的区域。
example.pinyin: Dìtú shàng biāo chū le yī piàn wèizhī de qūyù.
example.english: The map marked out an area of unknown territory.
example.fact: More than 80% of the world's oceans remain unmapped, unobserved, and unexplored by humans, according to NOAA. We have better maps of the surface of Mars and the Moon than we do of the ocean floor beneath our own planet's waters.

examples.hanzi: 太空中还有很多未知的星球。
examples.pinyin: Tàikōng zhōng hái yǒu hěn duō wèizhī de xīngqiú.
examples.english: There are still many unknown planets in space.

examples.hanzi: 面对未知的未来，他感到既期待又紧张。
examples.pinyin: Miànduì wèizhī de wèilái, tā gǎndào jì qīdài yòu jǐnzhāng.
examples.english: Facing an unknown future, he felt both excited and nervous.

components.note: 求 (seek) — the original picture of a fur coat (裘 qiú adds 衣); "seek, request" is a borrowed use. 求 sounds out 球 qiú and 救 jiù.
攵 (tap, hand with stick) — actions taken on something: 教, 放, 改; 救 is to take action to rescue.
求 (qiú) is a near sound match for jiù; 求 also means ask for help.

example.hanzi: 船员发出信号求救。
example.pinyin: Chuányuán fāchū xìnhào qiújiù.
example.english: The crew sent out a signal to seek help.
example.fact: The distress call 'SOS' was adopted internationally in 1906 not because it stands for any phrase, but because its Morse code pattern — three dots, three dashes, three dots — is simple and unmistakable to transmit and recognize under pressure, even for an untrained operator.

examples.hanzi: 她拿起手机向警察求救。
examples.pinyin: Tā ná qǐ shǒujī xiàng jǐngchá qiújiù.
examples.english: She picked up her phone and called the police for help.

examples.hanzi: 山里迷路的人用哨子发出求救信号。
examples.pinyin: Shān lǐ mílù de rén yòng shàozi fāchū qiújiù xìnhào.
examples.english: The person lost in the mountains used a whistle to send a distress signal.

components.note: 走 (walk, run) — movement: 起, 超, 趣, 赶; 越 is to cross over, to exceed.
戉 (yuè) sounds exactly like 越.
犭 (animal, dog) — animals, as in 狗 dog, 猫 cat, 狂 wild: dogs guard.
讠 (speech) — words and law; 狱 first meant a lawsuit, then a prison.

example.hanzi: 那名囚犯计划从监狱越狱。
example.pinyin: Nà míng qiúfàn jìhuà cóng jiānyù yuèyù.
example.english: That prisoner planned to break out of the prison.
example.fact: Alcatraz Federal Penitentiary in San Francisco Bay was long marketed as escape-proof, yet in 1962 three inmates carved through cell walls with spoons, built dummy heads from soap and hair to fool guards, and vanished on a makeshift raft; their fate was never conclusively determined.

examples.hanzi: 电影里的主角成功越狱了。
examples.pinyin: Diànyǐng lǐ de zhǔjué chénggōng yuèyù le.
examples.english: The hero in the movie successfully broke out of prison.

examples.hanzi: 警察抓回了三名越狱的犯人。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngchá zhuā huí le sān míng yuèyù de fànrén.
examples.english: The police caught three escaped prisoners.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 讠 is the simplified 言 (speech), as in 说, 话, 读; 讲 is to talk and explain.
井 (jǐng) — near sound — 讲 is jiǎng; the old form had a different right side, so this is only a loose hint.
辶 (movement, road) — 辶 marks going and moving, as in 过, 进, 送; 述 is following a story along, to narrate.
术 (shù) — same sound — 述 is shù, like 术 (art, technique).

example.hanzi: 这本小说讲述了一个渔村的故事。
example.pinyin: Zhè běn xiǎoshuō jiǎngshù le yī gè yúcūn de gùshi.
example.english: This novel tells the story of a fishing village.
example.fact: Homer's Odyssey, one of the oldest surviving works of Western literature at roughly 2,800 years old, was composed and transmitted orally for generations before it was ever written down, relying on rhythmic verse patterns that helped bards memorize thousands of lines.

examples.hanzi: 奶奶常常给我们讲述过去的故事。
examples.pinyin: Nǎinai chángcháng gěi wǒmen jiǎngshù guòqù de gùshi.
examples.english: Grandma often tells us stories from the past.

examples.hanzi: 他在演讲中讲述了自己的创业经历。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài yǎnjiǎng zhōng jiǎngshù le zìjǐ de chuàngyè jīnglì.
examples.english: In his speech he recounted his experience of starting a business.

components.note: 钅 (metal, simplified 金) — metals and tools: 钱, 钢, 铁; 键 is a metal bar or key.
建 (jiàn) sounds exactly like 键; also in 健 jiàn.

example.hanzi: 请按一下这个键。
example.pinyin: Qǐng àn yíxià zhège jiàn.
example.english: Please press this key.
example.fact: 键 is the key of a keyboard or piano, and gives 键盘 (keyboard), 按键 (button) and 化学键 (chemical bond). 关键 (the crucial point) uses it in a different sense.

examples.hanzi: 键盘上的有些键不灵了。
examples.pinyin: Jiànpán shàng de yǒuxiē jiàn bù líng le.
examples.english: Some of the keys on the keyboard have stopped working.

examples.hanzi: 关键时刻，他没有放弃。
examples.pinyin: Guānjiàn shíkè, tā méiyǒu fàngqì.
examples.english: At the crucial moment, he did not give up.

components.note: 多 (many) — two 夕 stacked, repeated again and again: so "many, much, more".
攵 (tap, strike) — 攵 marks an action, here counting; as in 教, 放.
娄 (lóu) — loose hint — 数 is shù; 娄 also sounds out 楼 lóu.

example.hanzi: 多数与会者都同意这个方案。
example.pinyin: Duōshù yùhuìzhě dōu tóngyì zhège fāng'àn.
example.english: The majority of attendees agreed with this proposal.
example.fact: In many parliamentary democracies, a 'supermajority' of two-thirds is required to amend a constitution — the same two-thirds threshold the US Congress needs to override a presidential veto, a deliberately high bar designed to force broad consensus before fundamental rules can change.

examples.hanzi: 多数人都喜欢周末睡懒觉。
examples.pinyin: Duōshù rén dōu xǐhuan zhōumò shuì lǎnjiào.
examples.english: Most people like to sleep in on weekends.

examples.hanzi: 投票结果由多数人的意见决定。
examples.pinyin: Tóupiào jiéguǒ yóu duōshù rén de yìjiàn juédìng.
examples.english: The vote result is decided by the majority's opinion.

components.note: 真 (zhēn) is a sound clue for 镇 zhèn and 慎 shèn; 真 means real, true.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.

example.hanzi: 这个动画角色后来被真人演员搬上了银幕。
example.pinyin: Zhège dònghuà juésè hòulái bèi zhēnrén yǎnyuán bān shàng le yínmù.
example.english: This animated character was later brought to the screen by a real-life actor.
example.fact: The 2019 live-action remake of The Lion King used no traditional cameras at all — every scene was generated inside a virtual-reality game engine, with filmmakers wearing VR headsets to 'walk' through a photorealistic digital savanna and frame shots as if filming real animals.

examples.hanzi: 这个游戏有真人表演的视频。
examples.pinyin: Zhège yóuxì yǒu zhēnrén biǎoyǎn de shìpín.
examples.english: This game has live-action videos with real people.

examples.hanzi: 这座蜡像和真人几乎一模一样。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò làxiàng hé zhēnrén jīhū yīmú yīyàng.
examples.english: This wax figure is almost identical to a real person.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh, 肉月旁) — the body-part radical, as in 脸, 腿, 脑; 胸 is the chest.
匈 (xiōng) gives the sound exactly: 胸 xiōng.
口 (mouth) — a picture of an open mouth; as a radical it appears in characters of speech, eating and sounds — 吃, 喝, 叫, 吗.

example.hanzi: 他跑完步后感觉胸口发闷。
example.pinyin: Tā pǎo wán bù hòu gǎnjué xiōngkǒu fā mèn.
example.english: He felt tightness in his chest after finishing his run.
example.fact: The human heart sits slightly left of center in the chest and beats roughly 100,000 times a day, pumping about 2,000 gallons of blood — enough to fill a small backyard swimming pool — through nearly 60,000 miles of blood vessels.

examples.hanzi: 他捂着胸口，说心里很难受。
examples.pinyin: Tā wǔ zhe xiōngkǒu, shuō xīnlǐ hěn nánshòu.
examples.english: He held his chest and said he felt terrible.

examples.hanzi: 小孩把脸埋在妈妈的胸口睡着了。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎohái bǎ liǎn máizài māma de xiōngkǒu shuì zháo le.
examples.english: The child buried his face in his mother's chest and fell asleep.

components.note: 人 (person) — the top. Common reading: a person standing between two sides, a go-between, as in 介绍 to introduce. Early forms may be armour.
八 (eight, divide) — Dictionary: a border dividing people. Memory aid: a person in the middle of two divided parts — in between.
入 (enter) — a pointed shape pushing in; not 人 (person), whose strokes spread outward.

example.hanzi: 警方及时介入,阻止了冲突升级。
example.pinyin: Jǐngfāng jíshí jièrù, zǔzhǐ le chōngtū shēngjí.
example.english: The police intervened in time, preventing the conflict from escalating.
example.fact: The 1962 Cuban Missile Crisis brought the US and Soviet Union to the brink of nuclear war; declassified records later revealed that a single Soviet submarine officer, Vasili Arkhipov, refused to authorize a nuclear torpedo launch during a tense standoff, a decision historians credit with averting catastrophe.

examples.hanzi: 我不想介入你们两个人的争吵。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bù xiǎng jièrù nǐmen liǎng gè rén de zhēngchǎo.
examples.english: I don't want to get involved in the argument between you two.

examples.hanzi: 政府决定介入这次劳资纠纷。
examples.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ juédìng jièrù zhè cì láozī jiūfēn.
examples.english: The government decided to step into this labor dispute.

components.note: 车 (vehicle, simplified 車) — the left part, as in 轮 wheel, 辆; the right part 欠 is no real sound clue for ruǎn.
亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 位.
牛 (ox) — in the traditional reading, a person 亻 dividing up an ox: one piece, hence 件 as a measure word for items.

example.hanzi: 这家公司开发了一款很受欢迎的软件。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī kāifā le yī kuǎn hěn shòu huānyíng de ruǎnjiàn.
example.english: This company developed a very popular piece of software.
example.fact: The term 'software' was first used in print in 1958 by statistician John Tukey, who coined it to distinguish programs from the physical 'hardware' of a computer — a distinction that didn't fully catch on in common usage until the personal computer boom of the late 1970s and 1980s.

examples.hanzi: 你的电脑上安装了什么软件？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ de diànnǎo shàng ānzhuāng le shénme ruǎnjiàn?
examples.english: What software is installed on your computer?

examples.hanzi: 这个软件需要每年更新一次。
examples.pinyin: Zhège ruǎnjiàn xūyào měinián gēngxīn yī cì.
examples.english: This software needs to be updated once a year.

components.note: 礻 (altar, spirit — form of 示) — rites and blessings: 神, 礼, 祝, 祈; 福 is good fortune from the gods.
畐 (fú) sounds exactly like 福; also in 幅 fú, 副 fù, 富 fù.
牛 (ox) — cattle and animals, as in 物 thing, 牧 herd, 牺 sacrifice: 特 first meant a bull, then special.
寺 (sì) is only a loose sound clue for tè; 寺 also in 诗 shī and 持 chí.

example.hanzi: 福特汽车公司成立于1903年。
example.pinyin: Fútè qìchē gōngsī chénglì yú 1903 nián.
example.english: Ford Motor Company was founded in 1903.
example.fact: Henry Ford didn't invent the automobile or the assembly line, but by adapting moving assembly-line techniques to car manufacturing in 1913, he cut the time to build a Model T from about 12 hours to roughly 90 minutes, making cars affordable to ordinary workers for the first time.

examples.hanzi: 我爸爸开的是一辆旧福特。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bàba kāi de shì yī liàng jiù Fútè.
examples.english: My dad drives an old Ford.

examples.hanzi: 福特先生是我们公司新来的经理。
examples.pinyin: Fútè xiānsheng shì wǒmen gōngsī xīn lái de jīnglǐ.
examples.english: Mr. Ford is our company's new manager.

components.note: 凵 (open pit) — oldest form shows a foot stepping out of a pit or cave: to go out, come out.
自 (self) — picture of a nose; Chinese speakers point to the nose to mean "I", so it became "self" (compare 鼻 bí, nose, which adds 畀).

example.hanzi: 这句名言出自一位古代哲学家。
example.pinyin: Zhè jù míngyán chūzì yī wèi gǔdài zhéxuéjiā.
example.english: This famous quote comes from an ancient philosopher.
example.fact: The phrase 'survival of the fittest' is often attributed to Charles Darwin, but he never coined it himself — it actually comes from philosopher Herbert Spencer, who used it in 1864 to summarize Darwin's theory of natural selection, and Darwin only adopted the phrase in later editions of On the Origin of Species.

examples.hanzi: 这个故事出自一本很有名的古书。
examples.pinyin: Zhège gùshi chūzì yī běn hěn yǒumíng de gǔshū.
examples.english: This story comes from a very famous ancient book.

examples.hanzi: 这些作品都出自同一位设计师之手。
examples.pinyin: Zhèxiē zuòpǐn dōu chūzì tóng yī wèi shèjìshī zhī shǒu.
examples.english: These works are all by the same designer.

components.note: 平 (píng, flat) also lends its sound to 评 píng, 苹 píng and 坪 píng.
⺮ (bamboo) — bamboo slips arranged in an even row; 等 means "rank, equal" and then "wait".
寺 (sì) is only a loose sound clue for děng; 寺 also in 诗 shī and 持 chí.

example.hanzi: 宪法规定所有公民在法律面前平等。
example.pinyin: Xiànfǎ guīdìng suǒyǒu gōngmín zài fǎlǜ miànqián píngděng.
example.english: The constitution stipulates that all citizens are equal before the law.
example.fact: New Zealand became the first self-governing country to grant women the right to vote nationally, in 1893 — nearly three decades before the United States did so in 1920 and more than fifty years before France, which did not grant women suffrage until 1944.

examples.hanzi: 男女应该享有平等的机会。
examples.pinyin: Nánnǚ yīnggāi xiǎngyǒu píngděng de jīhuì.
examples.english: Men and women should have equal opportunities.

examples.hanzi: 在朋友之间，大家都是平等的。
examples.pinyin: Zài péngyou zhījiān, dàjiā dōu shì píngděng de.
examples.english: Among friends, everyone is equal.

components.note: 彳 (step) — left half of a crossroads: 行 pictures a crossroads, so to go, and (háng) a row or trade.
一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.
辶 (walk) — movement and roads, as in 过, 近, 送: a way through.
甬 (yǒng) is a close sound clue for tōng; 甬 also in 痛 tòng, 桶 tǒng and 勇 yǒng.

example.hanzi: 这个计划在实际操作中行不通。
example.pinyin: Zhège jìhuà zài shíjì cāozuò zhōng xíngbutōng.
example.english: This plan won't work in actual practice.
example.fact: Prohibition in the United States, which banned the sale of alcohol from 1920 to 1933, is widely cited by economists and historians as a policy that simply didn't work — it fueled a massive black market, empowered organized crime syndicates, and was ultimately repealed after 13 years.

examples.hanzi: 这样做行不通，我们得换个方法。
examples.pinyin: Zhèyàng zuò xíng bu tōng, wǒmen děi huàn gè fāngfǎ.
examples.english: This won't work, so we have to change the method.

examples.hanzi: 老办法在新环境里行不通了。
examples.pinyin: Lǎo bànfǎ zài xīn huánjìng lǐ xíng bu tōng le.
examples.english: The old way no longer works in the new environment.

components.note: 辶 (walk, 走之旁) — movement and roads: 过 pass, 进 enter, 送 send; to follow is to move along behind someone.
后 (after, behind) — two words merged in simplified writing: old 后 "ruler" (皇后 empress) and 後 "behind, later" (as in 然后).

example.hanzi: 他先做了自我介绍,随后开始了演讲。
example.pinyin: Tā xiān zuò le zìwǒ jièshào, suíhòu kāishǐ le yǎnjiǎng.
example.english: He first introduced himself, and then began his speech.
example.fact: Total solar eclipses often trigger a rapid sequence of atmospheric changes: temperatures can drop by 10 degrees Fahrenheit or more within minutes of totality, and afterward, as the sun re-emerges, winds and temperatures snap back close to normal within about half an hour.

examples.hanzi: 他吃完早饭，随后就出门了。
examples.pinyin: Tā chī wán zǎofàn, suíhòu jiù chūmén le.
examples.english: He finished breakfast and went out soon afterward.

examples.hanzi: 你先走，我随后就到。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ xiān zǒu, wǒ suíhòu jiù dào.
examples.english: You go first, and I'll arrive right after.

components.note: 氵 (water) — slippery as wet surfaces; also in 河 river, 海 sea.
骨 (gǔ) is only a loose sound clue; 猾 huá shares it and sounds exactly like 滑.
雨 (rain) — weather radical, as in 雷 thunder, 雾 fog; snow is frozen rain.

example.hanzi: 他们每年冬天都去阿尔卑斯山滑雪。
example.pinyin: Tāmen měinián dōngtiān dōu qù Ā'ěrbēisī Shān huáxuě.
example.english: They go skiing in the Alps every winter.
example.fact: Skiing may be far older than commonly assumed — a rock carving in Norway dated to around 5,000 years ago depicts a person on skis, and wooden ski fragments preserved in Russian peat bogs have been carbon-dated to roughly 6,000 years old.

examples.hanzi: 我今年冬天打算学滑雪。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jīnnián dōngtiān dǎsuàn xué huáxuě.
examples.english: I plan to learn to ski this winter.

examples.hanzi: 滑雪的时候一定要戴头盔。
examples.pinyin: Huáxuě de shíhou yīdìng yào dài tóukuī.
examples.english: You must wear a helmet when skiing.

components.note: 心 (heart) — loyalty is of the heart, as in 想 think, 爱 love, 思; 心 sits at the bottom.
中 (zhōng) gives the sound exactly: 忠 zhōng, also in 钟 zhōng.

example.hanzi: 这只狗对主人很忠心。
example.pinyin: Zhè zhī gǒu duì zhǔrén hěn zhōngxīn.
example.english: This dog is very loyal to its master.
example.fact: 忠 is the Confucian virtue of loyalty, often paired with 孝 (filial piety). 忠诚 is 'loyal', 忠告 is 'advice', and 忠言逆耳 ('honest words grate on the ear') is a saying.

examples.hanzi: 他对朋友一向很忠诚。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì péngyou yíxiàng hěn zhōngchéng.
examples.english: He has always been loyal to his friends.

examples.hanzi: 这位老员工对公司忠心耿耿。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi lǎo yuángōng duì gōngsī zhōngxīn gěnggěng.
examples.english: This veteran employee is utterly loyal to the company.

components.note: 廾 (two hands) — two hands joined — 共 is doing together; it also sounds out 供 gōng.
口 (mouth) — 口 is the mouth, as in 吃, 喝, 叫; 和 is harmony and speaking together.
禾 (hé) — same sound — 和 is hé, like 禾.
尚 (shàng) gives the rhyme; 党 is a simplification of 黨, which was 尚 over 黑.

example.hanzi: 共和党在那次选举中赢得了多数席位。
example.pinyin: Gònghédǎng zài nà cì xuǎnjǔ zhōng yíngdé le duōshù xíwèi.
example.english: The Republican Party won a majority of seats in that election.
example.fact: The Republican Party's mascot, the elephant, was popularized by political cartoonist Thomas Nast in an 1874 Harper's Weekly illustration; Nast also independently popularized the donkey as the Democratic Party's symbol, and both images have stuck in American politics for a century and a half.

examples.hanzi: 共和党和民主党是美国的两大政党。
examples.pinyin: Gònghédǎng hé Mínzhǔdǎng shì Měiguó de liǎng dà zhèngdǎng.
examples.english: The Republican and Democratic parties are the two major parties in America.

examples.hanzi: 他一直是共和党的支持者。
examples.pinyin: Tā yīzhí shì Gònghédǎng de zhīchízhě.
examples.english: He has always been a Republican Party supporter.

components.note: 雨 (rain) — scattered raindrops, hence small bits and nothing; also in 雪 snow, 雷 thunder.
令 (lìng) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 铃 líng, 龄 líng and 领 lǐng.
亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 位.
牛 (ox) — in the traditional reading, a person 亻 dividing up an ox: one piece, hence 件 as a measure word for items.

example.hanzi: 这台机器缺少了一个重要零件。
example.pinyin: Zhè tái jīqì quēshǎo le yī gè zhòngyào língjiàn.
example.english: This machine is missing an important part.
example.fact: A modern jet engine like the GE9X, used on the Boeing 777X, contains over 30,000 individual parts, and airlines track many of them by unique serial number for their entire operational life so mechanics can trace the exact history of any single component.

examples.hanzi: 这辆自行车需要换一个新零件。
examples.pinyin: Zhè liàng zìxíngchē xūyào huàn yī gè xīn língjiàn.
examples.english: This bicycle needs a new part.

examples.hanzi: 工厂每天生产上千个汽车零件。
examples.pinyin: Gōngchǎng měitiān shēngchǎn shàng qiān gè qìchē língjiàn.
examples.english: The factory produces thousands of car parts every day.

components.note: 多 (many) — two 夕 stacked, repeated again and again: so "many, much, more".
人 (person) — the roof-like top. 余 absorbed 餘 (food left over); the shape no longer explains 'remainder'. Memory aid: a person with leftovers.
食 (food) — the old 餘 had the food part 饣; 余 is its sound part (yú), the same series as 除 chú, 徐 xú, 途 tú, with loose matches.

example.hanzi: 他觉得自己的解释显得多余。
example.pinyin: Tā juéde zìjǐ de jiěshì xiǎnde duōyú.
example.english: He felt that his explanation seemed unnecessary.
example.fact: The human appendix was long dismissed by biologists as a useless evolutionary leftover, but research published in the 2000s suggests it may act as a safe house for beneficial gut bacteria, helping repopulate the intestines after illnesses like cholera or dysentery wipe them out.

examples.hanzi: 这几句话是多余的，可以删掉。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jǐ jù huà shì duōyú de, kěyǐ shān diào.
examples.english: These sentences are unnecessary and can be deleted.

examples.hanzi: 房间里没有多余的椅子了。
examples.pinyin: Fángjiān lǐ méiyǒu duōyú de yǐzi le.
examples.english: There are no spare chairs in the room.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — marks actions done by hand, as in 打, 拉, 提; 援 is to lend a hand.
爰 (yuán) gives the sound exactly: 援 yuán, also in 暖 nuǎn and 缓 huǎn.
力 (strength) — effort, as in 办, 男, 努; 助 is to lend strength.
且 (qiě) is a loose sound clue for zhù; 且 also sounds out 祖 zǔ, 租 zū and 姐 jiě.

example.hanzi: 国际社会向灾区提供了大量援助。
example.pinyin: Guójì shèhuì xiàng zāiqū tígōng le dàliàng yuánzhù.
example.english: The international community provided substantial aid to the disaster area.
example.fact: The Marshall Plan, launched by the United States in 1948, provided over $13 billion (roughly $150 billion in today's dollars) to help rebuild sixteen war-torn Western European countries after World War II, and is widely credited with helping the region avoid economic collapse and the spread of famine.

examples.hanzi: 这家基金会给贫困学生提供援助。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā jījīnhuì gěi pínkùn xuésheng tígōng yuánzhù.
examples.english: This foundation provides aid to students in poverty.

examples.hanzi: 邻国派出医疗队援助受灾地区。
examples.pinyin: Línguó pàichū yīliáoduì yuánzhù shòuzāi dìqū.
examples.english: The neighboring country sent a medical team to help the disaster area.

meanings: sb who takes an exam for sb else

components.note: 木 (wood) — 枪 first meant a wooden spear; wood radical also in 棍 stick and 板 board.
仓 (cāng) hints at the sound — close to qiāng; the same part is in 抢 qiǎng and 苍 cāng.
手 (hand) — a picture of a hand with fingers spread. As a left-hand radical it becomes 扌 in 打 hit, 拿 take, 推 push.

example.hanzi: 警方正在追捕那名逃跑的枪手。
example.pinyin: Jǐngfāng zhèngzài zhuībǔ nà míng táopǎo de qiāngshǒu.
example.english: The police are pursuing the gunman who fled.
example.fact: Annie Oakley, one of history's most celebrated sharpshooters, could reportedly split a playing card edge-on from 30 paces and hit a dime tossed into the air; she toured with Buffalo Bill's Wild West show for 17 years, astonishing audiences across the US and Europe in the late 1800s.

examples.hanzi: 枪手逃跑后，警察封锁了街道。
examples.pinyin: Qiāngshǒu táopǎo hòu, jǐngchá fēngsuǒ le jiēdào.
examples.english: After the gunman fled, police sealed off the street.

examples.hanzi: 她被怀疑是替别人考试的枪手。
examples.pinyin: Tā bèi huáiyí shì tì biéren kǎoshì de qiāngshǒu.
examples.english: She was suspected of being a ringer who took the exam for someone else.

components.note: 生 (to grow) — old forms of 青 show fresh growing plants plus pigment; the colour is fresh blue-green. 青 also sounds out 清, 请, 情, 晴.
日 (sun) — spring is when the sun warms and plants sprout; also in 明 bright, 时 time.

example.hanzi: 这部电影讲述了几个年轻人的青春故事。
example.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng jiǎngshù le jǐ gè niánqīngrén de qīngchūn gùshi.
example.english: This movie tells the story of several young people's youth.
example.fact: Axolotls, a type of salamander native to Mexico, can regenerate entire lost limbs, portions of their spinal cord, and even parts of their heart and brain throughout their lives — an extraordinary form of biological youthfulness that has made them a major focus of regenerative medicine research.

examples.hanzi: 青春是一去不复返的美好时光。
examples.pinyin: Qīngchūn shì yī qù bù fù fǎn de měihǎo shíguāng.
examples.english: Youth is a beautiful time that never comes back.

examples.hanzi: 她把最美好的青春献给了教育事业。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ zuì měihǎo de qīngchūn xiàn gěi le jiàoyù shìyè.
examples.english: She devoted the best years of her youth to education.
